 Miles Bridges 
 PHX 
 Forward

 Miles Bridges tallied eight points (3-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, one steal and one blocked shot in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 Making his first official appearance in a Suns uniform, Bridges played 29 minutes in Wednesday’s 41-point defeat. The ankle injury he suffered early in the preseason may have played a role, with the Suns hoping to give Bridges more run to build his stamina. Unfortunately, he did little against the Trail Blazers’ deep reserves in what would be a lost night. As he showed in Charlotte, Bridges can provide solid category-league value, but it remains to be seen if that can carry over to Phoenix. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Miles Bridges (ankle) is out for the rest of Wednesday’s exhibition against the Bulls. 
 Bridges injured his right ankle during the first half of Wednesday’s game, ending his night after logging eight minutes. The veteran forward, whose arrival in Phoenix pushed Collin Gillespie out of the starting lineup, finished with three points, one rebound and one assist. However, Rasheer Fleming started the third quarter instead of Gillespie. Bridges’ injury did not appear serious, and the Suns won’t play their first regular-season game until October 21. 
 Miles Bridges 
 PHX 
 Forward 
 #0 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Hornets have traded Miles Bridges, a 2029 first-round pick and a 2027 second-round pick to the Suns for Grayson Allen, Royce O’Neale and a 2033 first-round pick. 
 With his draft rights acquired on the night of the 2018 NBA Draft, Bridges has spent his entire NBA career in Charlotte. He appeared in 77 games last season, averaging 17.1 points, 5.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 1.9 three-pointers while shooting 46.0 percent from the field and 82.2 percent from the foul line. His trade is the second for the Hornets in less than a week as the franchise charts a new path, with LaMelo Ball having been dealt to the Timberwolves on Wednesday. Bridges missed the entire 2022-23 season due to a (since-resolved) domestic abuse case, but has been a productive player when he’s suited up.. Bridges can provide solid fantasy value when available, but his ceiling will be capped in a lineup that features Devin Booker, Jalen Green and Dillon Brooks. 
 Miles Bridges 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #0 
 NBA insider Jake Fischer reports that the Hornets are “expected” to make Miles Bridges available via trade in conjunction with this month’s draft. 
 While there were some rumblings that Bridges could be had for the right price at the February trade deadline, the veteran forward remained in Charlotte. However, that may not be the case this summer, based on Fischer’s reporting. Bridges is going into the final year of his contract, with a $22.8 million cap hit. Regarding the draft, the Hornets currently hold two first-round picks, 14th and 18th overall. Would Bridges plus a pick be an approach for the team to take if they wanted to move up? That will be something to keep an eye on, especially with Charlotte also rumored to be seeking an upgrade at the center position. 
 Miles Bridges 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #0 
 Miles Bridges produced 15 points (5-of-12 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer in the loss to the Magic on Friday. 
 Bridges struggled with his three-point shot in the season-ending loss. However, his success inside the arc and at the charity stripe helped him finish as Charlotte’s second-leading scorer on the evening. Bridges didn’t contribute in many other areas, however, and a bad team performance prevented this contest from being competitive through the final horn. He ends his seventh NBA season with averages of 17.1 points, 5.8 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game. His fantasy production slipped this season, as did his overall numbers.

 Miles Bridges added 28 points (10-of-18 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), nine rebounds, two assists, one steal, three blocks and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Heat. 
 Bridges was exceptional on both ends of the floor during Tuesday’s contest. In his team-high 43 minutes, he did lots of damage from beyond the arc, but also had his share of buckets inside the three-point line. The veteran forward also battled on the glass and nearly amassed a double-double. But perhaps his biggest moment came in the closing moments of the game when he went up and blocked Davion Mitchell’s game-winning shot attempt to keep the Hornets’ season alive. Bridges totaled four stocks and will try to land another impactful two-way performance on Friday against the winner of Sixers-Magic.

 Miles Bridges had 25 points (10-of-12 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), eight rebounds, seven assists and four three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Timberwolves. 
 Bridges has now scored 25 points in two of his last three games and at least 19 points in four consecutive games. The 28-year-old small forward stepped up for the Hornets on a night when Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller combined for just 18 points. Bridges has provided eighth-round per game value over the last two weeks. The Hornets have three games in the last week of the regular season, starting with a matchup against the Celtics on Tuesday.

 One night removed from scoring 25 points in a win over the Suns, Bridges put up 19 more on Friday. Add in the assists and three-pointers, and this was another good performance for the Hornets’ forward. Bridges will look to end Week 23 on a high note when Charlotte visits Minnesota on Sunday.

 Miles Bridges tallied 25 points (10-of-16 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Thursday’s win over the Suns. 
 After scoring an efficient 19 points in Tuesday’s win over the Nets, Bridges was even better against the Suns. Recording his first 20-point game since March 14, the 25 were the most in a game for the Hornets’ forward since a March 11 win over the Kings (26 points). Add in the three-pointers, and Thursday was a good night for those rostering Bridges.

 Miles Bridges posted a full line on Tuesday with 19 points (7-of-12 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, four steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Nets. 
 Bridges set a new season high for steals, and he fell one swipe shy of matching his career high. Entering this game, Bridges had a quiet stretch, and this ended up being his highest-scoring performance since March 14. He’ll continue to start and play big minutes, but his box score production has at least partially been limited by lopsided scores. That wasn’t the case in this one, and he’ll look to stay hot against the Suns on Thursday.

 Miles Bridges produced 26 points (11-of-15 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Kings. 
 Bridges entered Wednesday’s game in a shooting slump, averaging 11.8 points per game on 30.8 percent shooting from the field over his last five games. To say he needed a night like Wednesday would be an understatement. The 26 points were the most Bridges has scored in a game since February 7, when he hit that number in a win over the Hawks. He’ll look to finish Week 20 on a high note when the Hornets visit the Spurs on Saturday.

 Gui Santos (leg) finished Saturday’s loss to the Suns with seven points (1-of-4 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, three assists and one three-pointer.
 Starting for Draymond Green, Santos played 23 minutes on Saturday. Unfortunately, an apparent left leg injury ended his night late in the third quarter. With the Warriors playing four games in Week 2, including a back-to-back, Santos could get another spot start, but only if he’s healthy. Keep an eye out for the injury report ahead of Monday’s game against the Nuggets.

 Trevon Brazile provided a boost off the bench with 17 points (6-of-101FGs), nine rebounds, one steal, two blocks and three three-pointers against the Pelicans on Saturday.
 With Cameron Johnson (ankle) sidelined, Bryce Hopkins got the starting nod in his place. However, he only played 19 minutes to Brazile’s 28, which led all reserves. Brazile wasn’t able to get much offense going in his debut, but he was able to knock down some big shots in this game, which included seven of Denver’s 15 points in overtime. The second-round pick is quickly looking like one of the better value picks from the summer, and he should be an important piece for Denver this season, though fantasy managers should exercise caution before adding the rookie. This level of production may not continue consistently. However, he absolutely deserves praise for his immediate production.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Jamal Murray led the Nuggets with 42 points (12-of-25 FGs, 10-of-13 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, one steal, one block and eight three-pointers in a 141-135 overtime win over the Pelicans on Saturday.
 After being held to just six points in the season opener, Murray bounced back in a big way in this game. He led Denver in scoring and accounted for over half of their three-pointers. He wasn’t able to get any offense going in overtime, but it was his heroics at the end of the game that forced the extra frame. He’ll look to carry this offensive production into Monday’s matchup with the Warriors, and fantasy managers shouldn’t expect to see many more six-point outings from him.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Nikola Jokić stuffed the stat sheet on Saturday with 35 points (12-of-23 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), 15 rebounds, 10 assists, two steals, three blocks, three three-pointers and six turnovers against the Pelicans.
 The first five quarters of Jokić’s season were rough, but he seems to have figured things out. He shot 1-of-5 and turned the ball over three times in the first quarter of this game, but he got back to producing at a high level after that. This was his first triple-double of the season, though he did need the extra five minutes to get there since seven of his boards came during overtime. He’ll continue to produce like a top-three player in fantasy basketball despite struggling in the season opener.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Dejounte Murray posted a full line on Saturday with 22 points (9-of-18 FGs), six rebounds, six assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Nuggets.
 It hasn’t resulted in a win yet, but Murray has been productive to start the season. His minutes are back up after being limited last season, and he’s shooting efficiently, unlike his first year with the Pelicans. Of course, he’s still contributing value across the board, and even with Jeremiah Fears starting, he still has the ball in his hands a ton. He’ll look to keep it going in the rematch with Denver on Wednesday.

 Trey Murphy led the Pelicans with 26 points (10-of-16 FGs), six rebounds, four assists, one steal and four three-pointers in a 141-135 overtime loss to the Nuggets on Saturday.
 Murphy struggled in the Pelicans’ first two games of the season, but he was able to get back on track in this one. He led New Orleans in scoring and surpassed his total points from the first two games. This type of performance was more in line with what he has been able to produce over the last two seasons, and he’ll look to keep it going in their next game, which will be a rematch with Denver on Wednesday.

 Derik Queen provided a boost off the bench with 17 points (6-of-10 FGs), eight rebounds and two assists against the Nuggets on Saturday.
 With Yves Missi (knee) sidelined for this game, head coach Jamahl Mosley opted to start DeAndre Jordan in his place. Jordan played 20 minutes, while Queen played 24 and was more productive, as expected. The Pelicans don’t play again until Wednesday, which is the first leg of a back-to-back. If Missi remains out, Queen should see a boost, and Jordan still wouldn’t be worth streaming.

 Josh Giddey accounted for nine points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Wizards.
 After shooting a combined 4-of-19 from the field in Chicago’s first two games, Giddey was considerably better on Saturday. Although he finished with just nine points, fantasy managers will be pleased with his rebounds and assists. Over three games, Giddey has shot 26.9 percent from the field and 50.0 percent from the foul line, numbers that must improve if he’s to justify his second-round ADP from the preseason.

 Norman Powell produced 18 points (4-of-12 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, four steals and three three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Wizards.
 Powell’s offensive role may be slightly larger than he anticipated when he signed with the Bulls, but it raises his fantasy ceiling. However, fantasy managers will reap the rewards only if he improves his accuracy. Through three games, Powell has shot 14-of-41 (34.1%) from the field, nearly 13 percentage points lower than his career number (47.0%). He’ll look to clean that up during the Bulls’ three-game Week 2, which starts on Monday in Boston.

 Matas Buzelis finished Saturday’s loss to the Wizards with 21 points (7-of-13 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 Buzelis had a difficult start to the season, totaling 24 points on 4-of-17 shooting. A 13-of-16 night at the foul line in the Bulls’ season-opening loss to the Raptors gave the point total a welcome boost. He was considerably better against the Wizards, shooting over 50 percent from the field and finishing a blocked shot shy of a complete stat line. Given what he’s being asked to do as one of the Bulls’ young building blocks, Buzelis’ field-goal percentage may struggle. That said, he’s still someone who should be rostered in all fantasy leagues.
